title: Network attestation flow — scenarios and lightweight PRD (ideation)
content:
Context and purpose:
This doc captures an ideation-level PRD for adding a lightweight network attestation and change-approval flow for customer-managed networking in Private deployments. Goal: give customers and ops teams a clear cryptographically-backed handshake and an auditable, machine-readable event trail that ties network changes to authorized approvals and enforced policies. This complements existing audit log work by focusing on the pre-change attestation and enrollment lifecycle (who signed off, what policy was applied, what proof exists).

Why this exists (problem statement):
- Customers running Redwood Private want predictable, auditable onboarding and change control for VPC peering, peered routes, and edge handshakes.
- Current audit logs record events after systems accept changes but there is no standardized attestable proof produced by the customer side that can be validated by Redwood control-plane when enrolling or applying config changes.
- SRE/ops and security reviewers need a short-lived, verifiable artifact (attestation token) that ties a change request to an approval and to the exact config diff applied. Without it, post-hoc forensics are slow and blame-prone.

Scope (what's in):
- Define an attestation token format (signed JSON) emitted by customer side operator tooling or a delegated admin agent.
- Define minimal approval metadata (approver id, approval ticket id, TTL, purpose, policy-id).
- Integrate attestation verification into the private control-plane change pipeline: reject changes missing valid attestations for gated operations.
- Extend audit-event schema to include attestation reference, signature verification status, and TTL expiration events.
- UI/CLI hooks: quick status of evidence, ability to replay proof for auditors.

Out of scope (for this iteration):
- Full PKI rollout for customers (we will initially accept customer-provided keys via KMS/HSM integration).
- Long-term storage and archive lifecycle policies beyond 1 year (platform-level retention will be handled separately).
- Deep policy language (we assume a small set of canonical policy types to start: emergency, scheduled-change, onboarding).

User personas and primary flows:
1) Platform Operator (customer) - "onboard-edge"
   - Runs local operator binary (or uses Terraform provider) to request an edge handoff.
   - The tool collects change metadata, optionally the Terraform plan diff, and produces an attestation JSON that is signed with customer-managed key (KMS/HSM).
   - The operator includes approval metadata (link to ticket, approver email or svc-account) and requests Redwood to validate the attestation during onboarding.

2) Customer Security Reviewer - "approve-route-change"
   - Uses internal approval system (Jira/ServiceNow) to approve a change. The approval system issues an approval token or records a ticket id; the operator includes that reference in the attestation.

3) Redwood Control Plane - "validate-and-apply"
   - Receives the change + attestation. Verifies signature using configured public key, validates ticket id via linked_artifacts (optionally calls back to customer system if configured), checks TTL and policy-id.
   - Emits audit event with fields: attestation_ref, signature_ok, approver_id, ticket_id, applied_by, change_hash.

Attestation token (MVP schema suggestion):
- attestation_version: v1
- change_hash: sha256 of normalized change payload (string)
- change_type: {"onboard-edge","route-update","peering-create"}
- approver: {"type":"email|svc","id":"alice@example.com"}
- approval_ticket: "JIRA-1234" (opaque)
- policy_id: "scheduled-window-default"
- issued_at: ISO8601
- expires_at: ISO8601
- signer_key_id: "projects/..../keys/customer-topkey"
- signature: base64(sig_over_canonical_payload)

Notes on canonicalization:
- We need a deterministic canonicalization step (strip whitespace, sort keys) so change_hash and signature validation are robust across toolchains. Recommend use of JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS) for v1.

Verification outcomes and audit events:
- attestation_verified: boolean
- verification_reason: string ("ok", "signature_mismatch", "expired", "unknown_key", "policy_violation")
- audit_payload: free text summary + link to raw attestation stored as evidence blob (S3/GCS).
- If verification fails, Redwood should produce a preventative outcome: reject, require manual override, or escalate to SOC.

Approval gate variants (MVP):
- Zero-touch: scheduled changes with signed attestations where approver is a service account and TTL is within acceptable window -> auto-approve.
- Manual-gated: require human approver ticket id and active check against customer's approval system (optional callback).
- Emergency bypass: require two distinct approver signatures and a captured justification in the attestation payload.

Telemetry and observability requirements:
- Instrument metric: attestation_verification_latency (histogram) and attestation_verification_success_rate (per change_type).
- Log structured events: attestation.received, attestation.verified, attestation.expired, attestation.rejected. Include trace-id to join with change application pipeline.
- Add UI surface in Console -> Private -> Changes to show: attestation status, approver, ticket link, signature key id, and raw blob download.

Security and key management considerations:
- Support two options for customer signing material: 1) customer-managed KMS public key uploaded to Redwood control-plane during tenant setup; 2) SSH-style manual public key upload for early adopters.
- Do not accept raw symmetric keys. Enforce asymmetric signing (RS/EC).
- Proof-of-possession: include signer_key_id in attestation and verify that submitted signature corresponds.
- Replay mitigation: change_hash + expires_at with short TTL (recommend default 30 minutes for operational changes, longer for onboarding flows).

Retention, compliance and privacy notes:
- Evidence blobs (raw attestations) stored encrypted at rest, retention default 90 days for operational changes, 365 days for onboarding. Hooks to longer-retention exports (S3 or customer archive) via customer-configured lifecycle.
- Mask any secrets that may accidentally appear in change payloads before storing raw blobs (implement a sanitizer that removes AWS keys, tokens, and PII heuristics).

Operational runbooks (high level):
- Failure case: signature_mismatch -> do not apply change, notify requestor, open ticket automatically in org queue.
- Expired token -> surface in UI with "re-request attestation" link that populates the operator CLI for re-signing.
- Verification service down -> degrade to manual-review path with strong audit markers and optional rollback if timeout reached.

Open questions / unresolved design decisions:
- Do we require Redwood to validate approval_ticket by calling customer approval system (callback) or accept opaque ticket ids and let customers provide an SLA that ensures ticket integrity? (trade-off: complexity vs assurance)
- Schema evolution: how to support cross-version attestation verification (v1 v2) and key rotation without invalidating existing evidence?
- Should we adopt an external standard (e.g., in-toto or sigstore) instead of a custom format? (pro: interoperability; con: heavier integration)
- How granular should policy_ids be for automated gating? Per-change-type only, or down to route-prefix and attribute-level policies?

Planned milestones (proposal):
- Week 0–2: finalise v1 attestation schema, canonicalization rules, and key registration UX.
- Week 3–6: implement verification service and audit-event integration + Console proof-of-concept.
- Week 7–10: add operator CLI integration (basic attestation generation), docs and runbooks.
- Week 11–14: alpha test with 2 customers (SLA-signed pilot), collect telemetry, iterate.

Next steps (action items):
- Priya: draft spec for canonicalization and choose signing scheme (RS/EC) by 2024-11-12.
- Ethan: spike minimal verification microservice and sample key registration API by 2024-11-19.
- Lina: prototype Console attestation viewer component and wireframe by 2024-11-26.
- Schedule a sync with Solutions Eng to select 2 pilot customers and confirm support constraints.

Appendix: example attestation (compact):
{"attestation_version":"v1","change_hash":"e3b0c442...","change_type":"route-update","approver":{"type":"email","id":"alice@example.com"},"approval_ticket":"JIRA-944","policy_id":"scheduled-window-default","issued_at":"2024-11-05T18:12:00Z","expires_at":"2024-11-05T18:42:00Z","signer_key_id":"projects/cust-1/keys/edge-ops-key","signature":"BASE64SIG=="}

Notes to reviewers: treat this as an ideation skeleton. We expect multiple iterations and a potential integration path with existing audit log PRDs. Feedback wanted on: canonicalization choice, TTL defaults, and whether we should require customer callback validation for ticket ids in MVP.

Changelog:
- 2024-11-05 Priya created initial ideation draft.
- 2024-11-20 Added approval gate variants and telemetry list (collab: Ethan).
- 2025-01-12 Incorporated pilot milestone and retention defaults (collab: Lina).
